notes: USMLE musculoskeletal outline supports genetic bone-remodeling disorders.

NLM-indexed CA2 literature supports the characteristic osteopetrosis, renal tubular acidosis, and cerebral calcification syndrome; the osteoclast acidification mechanism is consistent with carbonic-anhydrase-dependent proton generation.

exact_locator_notes: USMLE Content Outline — Musculoskeletal System, metabolic/genetic bone disorders.
Carbonic anhydrase II deficiency syndrome — PubMed abstracts documenting CA2 mutations and osteopetrosis/RTA/cerebral calcification.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The triad of osteopetrosis, renal tubular acidosis and cerebral calcification with biallelic CA2 loss identifies carbonic anhydrase II deficiency; impaired osteoclast proton generation reduces resorption-lacuna acidification and mineral dissolution.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: CTSK loss impairs collagen proteolysis after acidification; RANK affects osteoclast formation, ALPL impairs mineralization, and COL1 defects cause osteogenesis imperfecta rather than CA2 syndrome.
